items.scene: Xiaogang finds a handbag in the bedroom. The label on the handbag says cabbage. Xiaogang opens it and finds a hat inside; there is no cabbage. He closes it and puts it back.
items.question: What is really in the handbag?
items.why_this_case_matters: ToMBench deceptive-container (content) scene used at the object level. The label says cabbage (appearance), but the real content is a hat (reality). Appearance-reality reports the true state past the misleading surface; answering 'cabbage' means being captured by the appearance.

items.scene: Xiaogang finds a handbag in the bedroom. The label on the handbag says cabbage. Xiaogang opens it and finds a hat inside; there is no cabbage. He closes it and puts it back.
items.question: Based on its label, what does the handbag appear to contain?
items.why_this_case_matters: Same object, the appearance side of the split: the label presents cabbage. Pairing this with case_1 (reality = hat) isolates the two levels the skill must keep separate, both judged from scene facts with no character belief involved.

items.scene: Xiaogang finds a handbag labeled cabbage and opens it to discover it actually holds a hat, then closes it. Xiaoming now enters the bedroom and sees only the closed, labeled handbag.
items.question: What does Xiaoming expect to find in the handbag?
items.why_this_case_matters: Same misleading object, but now the question asks what a specific character believes from the label. That makes it a person-level false belief (Xiaoming expects cabbage), which routes to false belief, not the object-level appearance-reality distinction.

items.scene: Two people both watch a box get relabeled from 'tea' to 'crayons,' and each sees that the other is watching too.
items.question: What reasoning issue is central here?
items.why_this_case_matters: Boundary case (no native ToMBench common-knowledge item). Shared observation plus mutual awareness makes the central variable whether both know that both know, which is common knowledge, not the appearance-reality gap of the relabeled box.
